Consumer and Business Sentiment 
After improving strongly through most of the first quarter in 2020, measures of consumer and 
business sentiment pulled back in March 2020 as social distancing and business closures took 
effect.  The Reuters/Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to 101.0 in February 2020, just shy 
of the 14-year high reached in 2018, the subsequently fell by more than 29 points.  This index 
has since trended higher, standing at 82.8 in early May 2021 but still about 18 points below its 
February 2020 level.  From February 2020, the Conference Board’s consumer confidence index 
plunged by 46.9 points to 85.7 in April 2020, reaching its lowest level since mid-2014.  This 
index has fluctuated over the past several months, but in March and April showed strong 
increases in confidence.  The April reading of 121.7 was less than 11 points below last year’s 
high.  On the business side, the National Federation of Independent Business’s (NFIB) small 
business optimism index was, as of February 2020, only 4.3 points below its all-time high
